claims.text: Google announced on March 18, 2025 [Source: ev-1], that it had agreed to acquire cloud-security firm Wiz for approximately $32 billion in an all-cash deal [Source: ev-1].
This transaction represented the largest acquisition in Google's history and followed Wiz’s rejection of a previous $23 billion offer from Google in July 2024 [Source: ev-1].

The primary driver for this acquisition was strategic; under Thomas Kurian, Google Cloud sought to close its security gap with competitors AWS and Azure by pursuing consolidation in the cloud-security sector [Source: ev-1].
The deal signaled that cloud-security consolidation is viewed as the next major battleground in the ongoing "cloud wars" [Source: ev-1].
Furthermore, it indicated a market bet on AI-driven cloud adoption serving as the key demand driver for these services [Source: ev-1].
Although announced in March 2025, the deal completed after shareholder and regulatory steps were finalized, with completion reported in July 2025 [Source: ev-1].
No evidence was retrieved this round.
